faculty.name: Karin Meadows
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Karin Meadows](/images/0fc57d52f4-meadows-karin-20201-p3p5726tqtvzxwx3jope8t4w9oqf4fbynzvja7pa) ## Karin Meadows Business Manager at Yuba River Public Waldorf Charter School, Grass Valley, CA. Her lifelong commitment to the study of humankind has led her from religion to philosophy to education – specifically, how educational institutions may serve the public good based on a developmental model of education.

faculty.name: Tomasa Mendoza
faculty.bio: ! [** ](/images/b3c5f692f5-tomasa-mendoza-e1722258018213.jpg)[ **](#) ## Tomasa Mendoza Tomasa Mendoza has been working with children and their families in a public Waldorf setting for over a decade. She has a Waldorf Teaching Certificate from the Rudolf Steiner Teacher Training Program and has looped through four classes, teaching grades fourth through eight. In addition to her class teacher role, Tomasa also works as a mentor teacher, guiding new teachers through their first years in public Waldorf education. In her free time, Tomasa enjoys being outdoors and spending time with her family.

faculty.name: Michaelann Murphy
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Michaelann Murphy](/images/816a85207f-michaelann-murphy-300x300.webp) [** ](/images/a7d182cc26-michaelann-murphy.webp)[ **](#) ## Michaelann Murphy Michaelann Murphy is a biodynamic farmer, Waldorf educator, and founder of Earth and Sky Farm Community. She holds a masters degree in Waldorf Education, and her teaching certification encompasses early childhood through high school. She is an experienced educator, having taught nursery, kindergarten, and grades children in a number of Waldorf and private schools. She is the prior director of several early childhood centers and farm based education programs. In addition to teaching, Michaelann has served in Waldorf schools as pedagogical chair, a member of governance groups, and as an early education mentor. Michaelann has long held educational circles and studies for the benefit of adults in community, through movement, parent education, therapeutic agricultural activities, and teacher enrichment. As a trained and experienced biodynamic farmer, she is passionate about creating and guiding programs for the healing of the earth and the

faculty.name: Sarah Nelson
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Sarah Nelson](/images/4cf47a8393-nelsonsarah-3-300x300.png) ## Sarah Nelson Sarah graduated from the Center for Anthroposophy and Antioch New England Graduate School twenty years ago. Since then she has taught at Haleakala Waldorf School in Maui, Hawaii, where she worked with students from pre-K to Grade 8. For the last five years, in addition to class teaching, she has served as leader for the Southern California and Hawaii region on AWSNA’s Leadership Council. In 2021, after completing an eight-year journey with her class in Maui, She returned to British Columbia for a sabbatical and to see what the future will bring.

faculty.name: David Newbatt
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of David Newbatt](/images/ca8a0ad807-david-newbatt.webp) ## David Newbatt David Newbatt, artist and teacher, works mainly in watercolors and pastels on paper, as well as multi-media board and murals. He has spent over forty years living in Camphill Communities throughout the UK, specializing in the education of people with special needs through the use of visual arts and drama. David has travelled widely, teaching in Waldorf schools and Camphill communities. In addition to exhibiting his art work throughout the UK and Europe, he has illustrated a number of books published by Wynstones Press. For more information and to see David’s work please click ** [here.](https://cargocollective.com/davidnewbatt)**

faculty.name: Michal Noer
faculty.bio: ![Michal Noer](/images/f3f5c1f726-michal-noer-253x300.jpg) [** ](/images/8be829c747-michal-noer-e1721664725580.jpg)[ **](#) ## Michal Noer Four Year Certificate, Sculpture, Pennsylvania Academy of Fine Arts BFA, University of Pennsylvania Waldorf High School Teacher Training Certificate, Center for Anthroposophy Michal currently teaches a wide variety of different fine and practical arts at High Mowing School in Wilton NH, where she has worked in the High School since 2006. She holds a 4 Year Certificate in Sculpture from the Pennsylvania Academy of Fine Arts, and a BFA from the University of Pennsylvania. She completed the Waldorf High School Teacher Training through the Center For Anthroposophy in 2014. Michal is an alum of Kimberton Waldorf School and spent 8 amazing years of her childhood as a staff child at Camphill Village Kimberton Hills in Pennsylvania.

faculty.name: Geoff Norris
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Geoff Norris](/images/7317033725-geoff-norrisadobeexpress.webp) [** ](/images/7317033725-geoff-norrisadobeexpress.webp)[ **](#) ## Geoff Norris Geoff Norris trained in English and German Creative Speech graduating in 1978. He has toured with many groups worldwide as storyteller, speaker, actor and workshop leader, and was co-founder of The Rose Theatre Company, Portal Productions and Ashdown Eurythmy in the 1980 and 90’s. He has taught speech in many varied anthroposophical trainings and initiatives and was resident Speech and Drama consultant at Michael Hall School, Forest Row for more than 18 years mentoring teachers and children alike. He currently teaches, directs, acts and gives workshops, live and on Zoom, in the UK and abroad, including training students to achieve a Goetheanum recognized Steiner Creative Speech Diploma.

faculty.name: Colleen O'Connors
faculty.bio: ! [** ](/images/1e4732b172-colleen-oconner.png)[ **](#) ## Colleen O'Connors Born and raised in the USA, Colleen followed her studies and heart to Basel, Switzerland in 1980, remaining there for the next 24 years. Her daughter led her to Waldorf education and her daughter’s class teacher to the Hochschule für anthroposophische Pädagogik in Dornach, where she completed her Waldorf teacher training in 1995. After several years of working as an ESL-teacher and middle-school class teacher, Colleen returned to the US with her practical arts-teaching husband, furthering her teaching experience by becoming a class teacher at the Meadowbrook Waldorf School in RI and a high school teacher at High Mowing. During that time, she raised a son, bred Finn sheep, completed her Masters in Waldorf Education at ANE, began her work as mentor, evaluator, and adult educator, working in the Building Bridges and Exploration programs, as well as in the Antioch Teacher Training Summer Intensives. In 2021 they returned to Switzerland and she to her first calling as a middle school and ESL teacher at the Rudolf Steiner Schule Zürcher Oberland. They are both newly

faculty.name: Dick “Cedar” Oliver
faculty.bio: ![Dick Cedar Oliver](/images/df64ddf1e4-dick-cedar-oliver-300x300.jpg) ## Dick “Cedar” Oliver A science, math, technology, digital arts and design teacher in Waldorf high schools and middle schools for over 20 years, Cedar is also the author and co-author of numerous books and software titles and has worked with scientists, mathematicians, engineers and artists around the world. He attended the University of Maine and the University of Michigan in addition to the WHiStep Waldorf Teacher Education program and 5-year Spacial Dynamics training. In addition to his work on the CFA faculty, he currently serves as a visiting science teacher and faculty mentor at several U.S. Waldorf schools.

faculty.name: Charlie Orphanides
faculty.bio: ! ## Charlie Orphanides Charlie Orphanides is currently the 8th Grade Class teacher at the Denver Waldorf School. He served as the Education Director for the last two years and will return to that role after completing this school year. He has spent the last fifteen or so years as a class teacher, Games and Movement teacher, middle school math teacher, therapeutic movement specialist and circus arts teacher. Along with The Denver Waldorf School, Charlie has taught at the Brooklyn Waldorf School and Boulder Valley Waldorf School. In deepening his commitment to forwarding the work of anthroposophy in the world, he continues to immerse himself in the study of how and why we do what we do in Waldorf schools. He has also completed the 5-year In-Service training from the Spacial Dynamics Institute as well as a certification in Bothmer Gymnastics. After studying several modalities in intentional and therapeutic movement, Charlie has most recently immersed himself in a general study of somatic therapies and coaching, particularly around how to address the effects of trauma, both for individuals as well as in the classroom, including the Emergency Pedagogy courses with Bernd Ruf at the Ka

faculty.name: Sara Ciborski, Ph.D.
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Sara Ciborski](/images/8b065a1590-sara-ciborski-1.webp) ## Sara Ciborski, Ph.D. Sara Ciborski, Ph.D. has been a member of the Anthroposophical Society since 1984 and a First Class member since 1994. She has a B.A. in English from Smith College and an M.A. and Ph.D. in cultural anthropology from the University at Albany. She has served for many years on the Focus Group for the meditation workshops of Georg Kühlewind’s Logos Working Group (formerly Therapists’ Group). She has worked in development, writing grants for Camphill, AWSNA, and most recently for the Lakota Waldorf School on the Pine Ridge Lakota Indian Reservation. She is a Waldorf parent and grandparent and co-author of the research monograph *Assessment for Learning in Waldorf Classrooms: How Waldorf Teachers Measure Student Progress Toward Lifelong Learning Goals*. She lives in New Hampshire, at MorningSun, a Buddhist mindfulness education center founded by her son.

faculty.name: Torin Finser, Ph.D.
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Torin Finser](/images/911b9a0c34-torin-finser-cropped-1.jpg) ## Torin Finser, Ph.D. Torin M Finser, PhD, has served Waldorf education for over four decades, as class teacher and faculty chair at the Berkshire Waldorf School, director of teacher education at Antioch University, General Secretary of the Anthroposophical Society and a founder of the Center for Anthroposophy. His innovative efforts led to many new programs, including most recently Building Bridges and Waldorf Leadership Development. He is the author of 15 books, the most recent: Listening to our Teachers – Advocacy through Research (2024). Some of his other books have been translated into Portugese, Mandarin, Korean, Arabic, Spanish, and next year School as a Journey will appear in Greek. Torin and Karine are now enjoying nine grandchildren.

faculty.name: Douglas Gerwin, Ph.D.
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Douglas Gerwin](/images/19722bb846-254.jpg) ## Douglas Gerwin, Ph.D. Executive Director of the Center for Anthroposophy (CfA) Himself a Waldorf graduate, Douglas Gerwin, Ph.D., is Executive Director of the Center for Anthroposophy (CfA). He has taught history, literature, German, music, and life science at the university and Waldorf high school levels for over 40 years and helped prepare high school educators to teach these subjects for over a quarter-century. He is also an adjunct faculty member of the Waldorf Teacher Education Program at Antioch University New England. In 1996, he founded CfA’s Waldorf High School Teacher Education Program (WHiSTEP), a graduate-level training specifically for high school teachers, which he chaired for 27 years. During that time, he also served as advisor or mentor to well over three-quarters of the Waldorf high schools in North America and helped train Waldorf teachers on four continents. Editor of ten books and author of numerous articles on Waldorf education and anthroposophy, Dr. Gerwin is also Executive Director of the Research Institute for Waldorf Education (RIWE). A founding mem

faculty.name: Lori Kran, Ph.D.
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Lori Kran](/images/79585d2972-lori-kran-e1751297567922.png) ## Lori Kran, Ph.D. Lori earned a PhD in American and Women’s History from the University of Massachusetts, Amherst and her Waldorf teacher certification from the Waldorf Teacher Development Association in Ann Arbor, MI. Before her current role as the coordinator for PITEP (Pilot In-Service Teacher Education Program) Lori was the pedagogical director at Shining Mountain Waldorf School. Lori was a grades 1-8 Waldorf class teacher, Waldorf high school teacher, and university history/gender studies adjunct professor. Lori has served as an AWSNA delegate for 20+ years. Lori continues to serve as a mentor and as a visiting school evaluator to several Waldorf schools. She enjoys hiking in the Rocky mountains, gardening, reading novels, and playing her banjo!

faculty.name: Linda Williams, Ph.D.
faculty.bio: ![A portrait of Linda Williams](/images/4434d9a04a-download.jpg) ## Linda Williams, Ph.D. A class teacher for over 25 years, is currently in the 8th grade with her students at the Detroit Waldorf School. Dr. Williams received her Waldorf training at the Waldorf Institute of Mercy College and her doctorate in literacy education in 2006 from Michigan State University. Besides teaching at Detroit Waldorf, Dr. Williams also taught for 3 years at the Urban Waldorf School in Milwaukee, the first public Waldorf school in the United States. After serving for 8 years as an Associate Professor of Literacy in the Department of Teacher Education at Eastern Michigan University, Dr. Williams returned to the classroom at Detroit Waldorf, where she serves on the College, DEI and Pedagogical committees.

faculty.name: Thea Pratt
faculty.bio: ! [** ](/images/4186c5f579-thea-pratt-2-300x300-1.png)[ **](#) ## Thea Pratt Thea Pratt is the handwork teacher at the Waldorf School on the Roaring Fork in Carbondale, Colorado, where she is beginning her 20th year of teaching. A Waldorf alumna herself, Thea attended a Waldorf school in Minneapolis from seventh through twelfth grade. She went on to earn her bachelor’s degree in Studio Arts and German Studies from Wesleyan University, and completed her Waldorf teacher training at Antioch University in 2010. In addition to her work in education, Thea is also a professional chalk artist, known for her large-scale public installations in and around Aspen, Colorado. Her art can be viewed on Instagram at @roaringforkchalk

faculty.name: Laura Radefeld
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Laura Radefeld](/images/2035f18e96-laura-radefeld.jpg) ## Laura Radefeld Diploma, Eurythmy Spring Valley; Pedagogical Eurythmy Diploma, Emerson College, U.K. Teaches eurythmy at Green Meadow Waldorf School in Chestnut Ridge, NY. Adjunct faculty at Antioch University New England and teacher at School of Eurythmy in Spring Valley, NY. Regularly performs within the USA, including the Making Music Visible Tour and the Midwest Eurythmy Group. **CfA teaching:** Eurythmy in all three levels of the Waldorf High School Teacher Education Program.

faculty.name: Magnolia Rios
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Magnolia Rios](/images/ba3ba74557-magnolia-rios-300x300.webp) ## Magnolia Rios Magnolia is originally from Colombia, where her journey with anthroposphy began in 1991 when her son entered the Waldorf School in Cali. What began as a parent’s interest soon deepened into a committed path of study, reflection and understanding of the principles underlying Waldorf education. A trained Waldorf teacher with a specialty in World Languages – Spanish, Magnolia has been the Spanish teacher at The Waldorf School of Lexington in Massachusetts since 2001. During her tenure she has also served as Subject Teacher Chair, College of Teacher Chair, and as an AWSNA Delegate. With a background in Fine Arts, Graphic Design, and Early Childhood Education, she brings imagination, creativity, and aesthetic sensitivity to her teaching. Her ongoing professional and inner development continue to be guided by anthoposophical studies and practice. Magnolia is also a certified Biography and Social Art facilitator. In this capacity, she works not only with individuals and community groups, but also with school faculties, parents, and staff. Through gui

faculty.name: Kris Ritz
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Kris Ritz](/images/ce91a31383-ritz-kris2-300x300.jpg) ## Kris Ritz Kris Ritz joined the Emerson Waldorf School community in 2008 and has since journeyed through the grades there with two groups of students. Kris now enjoys the role of a pedagogical support teacher in which she works with grades 1 – 8 students in various capacities. Before returning to North Carolina, she was a class teacher at the Austin Waldorf School and spent a year at Plowshare Farm, an anthroposophical life-sharing community. Born in Upstate New York, Kris graduated from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism. During a career in advertising, she discovered Waldorf education, returned to school, and earned a Waldorf certificate and master’s degree from Antioch New England Graduate School. Whether supporting the efforts of the students in the classroom or working with the third grade teachers as it relates to the curriculum and the developmental threshold of the 9-/10-year change, Kris is inspired by the questions, answers, and “A-has!” that unfold while working and learning together in community.

faculty.name: Bernd Ruf
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Bernd Ruf](/images/51b35b4e70-portrait-of-bernd-ruf-300x300.jpg) ## Bernd Ruf Presenter, Founder of Parzival School & Emergency Pedagogy Author of Educating Traumatized Children, Bernd Ruf is the founder of the worldwide Emergency Pedagogy crisis intervention center, based in Karlsruhe, Germany. Skilled teams are sent out to help traumatized children in places of the strife of war, or ecological disasters.

faculty.name: Sven Saar
faculty.bio: ! ## Sven Saar Sven gained his Waldorf Teaching diploma as a very young man. After moving to England, he worked as a class teacher for 30 years, eight of those in Germany. He also taught in the High School, specializing in history and drama. Now he works full time in Teacher Education and is on the faculty of several courses and universities in the UK, Germany, Australia and the US. Sven gives lectures and seminars internationally and works as an active mentor and advisor to schools and teachers in many countries. He is a co-founder of *The Modern Teacher: Education as Art* (UK) and co-ordinates the [Waldorf 360 platform for High School teachers](https://modernteacher.org/waldorf-360).

faculty.name: Peter Selg
faculty.bio: ! [** ](/images/2ef5fe5afd-peter-selg.jpg)[ **](#) ## Peter Selg Peter Selg studied medicine in Witten-Herdecke, Zurich, and Berlin and, until 2000, worked as the head physician of the juvenile psychiatry department of Herdecke Hospital in Germany. Dr. Selg is director of the Ita Wegman Institute for Basic Research into Anthroposophy (Arlesheim, Switzerland), professor of medicine at the Alanus University of Arts and Social Sciences (Germany), and co-leader of the General Anthroposophical Section at the Goetheanum. He is the author of numerous books on Rudolf Steiner, anthroposophy, medical ethics, and the development of culture and consciousness.

faculty.name: Nikki Moon Shoneman
faculty.bio: ![a portrait of Nikki Shoneman](/images/8b61ce0587-nikki-shoneman-portrait-300x300.webp) [** ](/images/ed7085bbd4-nikki-shoneman-portrait.webp)[ **](#) ## Nikki Moon Shoneman Nikki Moon Shoneman is an artist, educator, and therapeutic guide with more than 30 years of professional experience integrating art, education, nature, and trauma-informed practices. Nikki holds a Master’s degree in Education and a Waldorf Grades teaching certificate from Antioch University, a Kairos Institute graduate, a Lifeways graduate in early childhood, and a BA in Fine Arts from UCSC. Nikki has completed Waldorf Leadership Development, Explorations, and is a Wilderness First Responder. Her professional background includes teaching from early childhood through graduate education, including serving as adjunct faculty and Fine Arts instructor at Antioch University, Kairos Institute, Building Bridges, and Explorations. She also serves with Emergency Pedagogy Without Borders, offering trauma-informed, art-based support to communities impacted by crisis. Throughout the year, Nikki teaches Fine Arts both in person and

faculty.name: Jinsook Song
faculty.bio: ! ## Jinsook Song Dr. Jinsook Song is a licensed marriage and family therapist and an American Association for Marriage and Family Therapy (AAMFT) approved supervisor. She joined AUNE as the Director of the clinical training for CFT MA and PhD programs in 2021 after previously serving as an adjunct instructor and supervisor. Dr. Song received her master’s in Music Therapy from New York University and PhD in Marriage and Family Therapy from AUNE. She brings many years of clinical experiences working with children, adults and older adults in school settings, integrated primary care settings, a community mental health agency and private practice. Her clinical and research interest areas are medical family therapy, trauma informed therapy, intergenerational trauma, child-parent psychotherapy, use of creativity in trauma work, community engagement in treatment, multicultural and feminist issues, cultural identity, supervision, and strengthening family relationships. She serves on the educational committee for NHAMFT.

faculty.name: Jeff Spade
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Jeff Spade](/images/ff62d344cc-spadejeff-637x1024-2-300x300.png) ## Jeff Spade Jeff, a member of the music and drama faculty at the Rudolf Steiner School in New York City, has been teaching music in Waldorf schools for over three decades. Prior to joining RSS, he was music director at Chicago Waldorf School and Kimberton Waldorf School. He has also worked as a guest teacher, mentor, and consultant with the Waldorf schools across the U.S. In addition to working in the classroom and conducting choirs and ensembles, Jeff is a composer (Eureka! The Life and Times of Archimedes: A Musical Play in One Act for grades 5-12) and a teacher of teachers, having led music classes at several Waldorf teacher training programs.

faculty.name: Tonya Stoddard
faculty.bio: ! [** ](/images/89d7a46fc2-tonya-stoddard.png)[ **](#) ## Tonya Stoddard Tonya Stoddard, LCSW, is a Licensed Clinical Social Worker with a Master’s in Social Work and completed the Anthroposophic Psychology program. Tonya has over 20 years of experience working in the San Francisco Bay Area and Sonoma County. She has worked psychotherapeutically with diverse populations and issues, including children and adolescents in both nonprofit and private practice settings. Currently, Tonya works as an Education Support Specialist at The Waldorf School of Tampa Bay in Tampa, FL. Tonya continues to work in private practice and collaboratively with the healing arts community. She is an adjunct faculty member of the Healing through Art program in California, a faculty member of the Association for Anthroposophic Psychology, and serving on the Leadership Team of the Anthroposophic Health Association.

faculty.name: Malina Stoychev
faculty.bio: ! ## Malina Stoychev With over 35 years of Waldorf teaching experience, Malina brings a deep love for the art of teaching and the growth of the human being. She has served as a class teacher at the Emerson Waldorf School in Chapel Hill, NC, for the past 16 years, where she is preparing to graduate her second class. Her teaching journey has also led her to the River Valley Waldorf School and to Waldorf and Camphill communities across two continents. Malina holds degrees in Elementary Education from Bulgaria and in Curative Education from Northern College, Aberdeen University, and Camphill Rudolf Steiner Schools in Scotland, with a second major in Art Therapy and Developmental Movement. She is passionate about weaving the principles of curative education and the Extra Lesson into classroom life, bringing healing, balance, and a deeper understanding of each child’s unique journey. As a mentor and colleague, she finds great joy in supporting other educators and learning from the diverse communities she visits. For the past decade, Malina has served as the AWSNA Delegate for the Emerson Waldorf School and has worked for over 16 years as an accreditation team member and chair for AW

faculty.name: Elizabeth Sustick
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Elizabeth Sustick](/images/ba4b0adfc1-elizabeth-sustick.webp) ## Elizabeth Sustick Elizabeth is a certified Anthroposophic Nurse Specialist, Rhythmical Einreibung Specialist, and Rhythmical Massage Therapist in a private caregiving practice in Northampton, MA, where she also enjoys her grandmother role to 5 grandchildren. She is the President of the North American Anthroposophic Nurses Association and a board member of the International Forum for Anthroposophic Nursing in Dornach, Switzerland.

faculty.name: Monica Talaya
faculty.bio: ![Monica Talaya Armstutz](/images/7f791b7002-monica-armstutz-1-300x300.jpeg) ## Monica Talaya Monica Talaya completed the Dorion School of Anthroposophical Music Therapy (AMT) in 2005, after her training as a Certified Music Practitioner. Since then, she has worked as an AMT with different populations, age groups and in varied settings, most consistently in the Camphill Communities. She also teaches the lyre to children (from 5 years old onward) and adults in groups and individually. Monica has given presentations about AMT and has lead courses and workshops for early childhood teachers and parents of young children about the importance of the ‘mood of the fifth’, providing an in-depth experience and understanding of the different stages of a child’s musical development and needs. She wishes to inspire parents for and teaches the singing of lullabies. Earlier in her life she trained to be a kindergarten- and later a special education teacher and raised her own five children.

faculty.name: Juliane Weeks
faculty.bio: ![Juliane Weeks](/images/431763bd01-juliane-weeks.jpg) ## Juliane Weeks Juliane Weeks has a diploma in anthroposophic music therapy, and is a Certified Music Practitioner and former Waldorf teacher. As music therapist, she has worked with individuals of all ages and abilities in many different settings, Waldorf Schools, Life Sharing Communities, Hospice, the Therapeutic Community Inner Fire and others. In addition to her therapeutic work, she has offered workshops, lead singing groups and music courses in the Camphill Academy, taught music in the Early Childhood teacher training at Sophia’s Hearth and in the Healing Education program (Med) at Antioch. Together, Juliane and Monica have led Renewal courses on Music in the Light of Anthroposophy.

faculty.name: Christof Wiechert
faculty.bio: ![Portrait of Christof Wiechert](/images/569e7cd849-christof-1-squareup-300x300.jpg) ## Christof Wiechert Christof Wiechert, a popular lecturer, author, and seminar leader the world over, spent 30 years teaching at the Waldorf School in The Hague, where he himself was a pupil. During this time, he co-founded the Dutch Waldorf Teacher Training Seminar. For many years, Christof was a council member in the Anthroposophical Society in the Netherlands. Together with Ate Koopmans, he developed the “Art of the Child Study” course. A number of his books are available in English translation. In 1999, he began to work for the Pedagogical Section of the Anthroposophical Society and, from 2001 to 2011, served as Leader of the Pedagogical Section of the School for Spiritual Science at the Goetheanum in Dornach, Switzerland. He is married with five children.

faculty.name: Nathan Wilcox
faculty.bio: ![Nathan Wilcox](/images/bc1a6e06c2-nathan-wilcox-.jpg) ## Nathan Wilcox Nathan Wilcox has taught English, history and drama and served as the High School Chair at the Waldorf School of San Diego since he founded its high school in 2008. Prior to becoming a Waldorf teacher Nathan worked as a social worker for adults with developmental disabilities. He holds a Bachelor of Arts in English from Pomona College in Claremont, California, and Jesus College in Cambridge, England. He completed his Waldorf High School teacher training in literature at Rudolf Steiner College under the direction of Betty Staley and John Wulsin. Nathan makes his home with his wife and children on the ancestral and unceded territory of the Kumeyaay people.

faculty.name: Eduardo Yi
faculty.bio: ! ## Eduardo Yi Eduardo Yi was born in Lima, Peru. Throughout his childhood and adolescence he experienced an unstable cultural and political environment : dictatorship, socialism, communism and democracy. These experiences awakened in him a number of questions pertaining to social issues. The most encompassing, the human being in relation to society. In the late seventies Eduardo met anthroposophy. During the late 80’s and early 90’s he became involved in the San Juan Anthroposophical Branch. He helped to start the Lima Waldorf School (1982), became Member of the Anthroposophical Society (1987), a member of the School of Michael (1989) helped to found the Christian Community (1990) and helped to found the Anthroposophical Society in Peru(1992). In the mid 90’s Eduardo became the administrator of the Lima Waldorf School. It was a tumultuous time. Eduardo enrolled in the Teacher Training at Sunbridge College in NY. He then spent a year teaching Spanish at the Summerfield Waldorf School in CA. During this time he also taught in the Schiller Goethe teacher training program in Lima.
